{{nihongo|'''Ojiharina Mawakahime Shrine'''|尾治針名真若比咩神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Bizen Province]].

=== Enshrined deity ===
* Ojiharinamawakahime-no-Mikoto

=== History ===
In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}}, the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' lists "Ojiharinamawakahime Shrine" in {{ill|Mino district|ja|御野郡|zh|御野郡|qid=Q11071226}} of {{ill|Bizen Province|bn|বাইজেন প্রদেশ|cs|Provincie Bizen|de|Provinz Bizen|es|Provincia de Bizen|fa|ولایت بیزن|fr|Province de Bizen|gl|Provincia de Bizen|id|Provinsi Bizen|it|Bizen (provincia)|ja|備前国|ko|비젠국|lt|Bidzeno žemė|nl|Bizen (provincie)|pt|Província de Bizen|ru|Бидзэн (провинция)|simple|Bizen Province|sk|Bizen (provincia)|sr|Провинција Бизен|tr|Bizen (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Бідзен|zh|備前國|zh_min_nan|Bizen-kok|qid=Q1053688}}, ranking it as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Bizen no Kuni Jinmyōchō}},' the Sōja manuscript records "Owari Harita Mawakahime Shrine," and the Yamamoto manuscript records "Junior Fourth Rank Lower Owari Harita Myōjin"<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.okayama-jinjacho.or.jp/cgi-bin/jsearch.cgi?mode=detail&jcode=01046 Ojiharinamawakahime Shrine] (Okayama Prefectural Shrine Association).</ref>.

Near this shrine is a mountain called "Handa-yama," said to be a mistaken form of "Harita-yama," and the name "Harita" is said to derive from this shrine<ref name="神社庁"/>. The shrine name suggests relation to the {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}}, also supported by nearby {{ill|Ohari Shrine|ja|尾針神社|qid=Q17226111}}, another Shikinaisha associated with the Owari clan. Related theories include westward migration of the Owari clan from Owari<ref>Recorded in the Meiji-period 'Engishiki Inner Shrines and Kokushi Existing Shrines' (Obari Shrine section in 'Gods of Japan - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyō and Shikoku' ({{ill|Hakusuisha Publishing|Q4346470|qid=Q4346470}})).</ref>, and conversely eastward migration from Kibi to Owari<ref>Hiroaki Shimoyama, "Were the ancient Owari clan migrants eastward from Kibi?" ('Okayama Prefecture Mystery Walks,' Shinjinbutsu Bunko).</ref>.

However, Ojiharinamawakahime Shrine was formerly worshiped at the present Misaki-gū site (Kitagata, Kita-ku, Okayama; {{ウィキ座標|34|41|05.76|N|133|56|04.24|E|region:JP-33_type:landmark|位置|name=Misaki-gū (former site)}}), where Amatsu Shrine had been worshiped<ref name="玄松子">[http://www.genbu.net/data/bizen/ojiharina_title.htm Ojiharinamawakahime Shrine] (Genmatsuko personal site).</ref>. After entering Meiji, Ojiharinamawakahime Shrine was moved here and Amatsu Shrine became a precinct end shrine<ref name="玄松子"/>.

Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, it was ranked {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.
